question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{x-3}}$ and the point $P(7,\frac{3}{4})$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(\frac{3}{4},7).$
question.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(7,\frac{3}{4}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{x-3}} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\frac{3}{4(x-3)^{3/2}} \\ {f}^{′}(7) & =-\frac{3}{32}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(7,\frac{3}{4})$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(\frac{3}{4},7)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(\frac{3}{4}) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(\frac{3}{4}))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(7)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-\frac{3}{32})} \\  & =-\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
